verdict.rationale: Airbyte documents incremental syncs that pull only data changed since the previous sync, and CDC replication that reads database change logs while tracking its current position, so new and changed records move without full reloads. A community user reports Airbyte continued syncing incrementally after the initial load. Missing for 10: explicit docs on how cursor fields and state are stored and managed automatically per connection, incremental mode docs beyond the Connector Builder context, and documented handling of hard deletes in cursor-based incremental mode.

support.subject: As a data engineer, syncs move only new and changed records — cursor and state management handled for me, not full reloads

citations.quote: An incremental sync is a sync which pulls only the data that has changed since the previous sync

A consumer of these log files (such as Airbyte) can read these logs while keeping track of the current position within the logs in order to read all record changes coming from DELETE/INSERT/UPDATE statements.
'tricked' Airbyte into thinking it had done the first sync. After that, it continued to sync happily.
